integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Live-action, deliberately overdramatic early-2000s romantic-comedy movie trailer titled "SEX AND THE CITY GOES TO MARS." Carrie Bradshaw and Samantha Jones are the only principal characters. Carrie Bradshaw has shoulder-length curly blonde hair, a slim figure, glamorous makeup, and wears an extravagant designer-style silver space suit with fashionable high-heeled space boots and a transparent bubble helmet. Samantha Jones has shoulder-length blonde hair, glamorous makeup, and wears a fitted metallic-gold designer-style space suit with matching boots and a transparent bubble helmet. They stand together inside an absurdly luxurious pink-and-silver spacecraft approaching MARS, with the enormous red planet filling the windows. A deep, gravelly male movie-trailer narrator (S1) says in an off-screen voiceover: <d>[English] This summer... two women are going where no Manhattan socialite has gone before.</d> while Carrie and Samantha's lips remain completely closed. [Shot 2] At 00:06.000, the camera cuts to Carrie and Samantha dramatically walking down the spacecraft ramp onto the dusty red surface of Mars. Their fashionable boots immediately sink awkwardly into the Martian dirt. Carrie looks down at her boots in horror. Carrie Bradshaw, with a sophisticated adult female voice (S2), says: <d>[English] Samantha, these boots are ruined.</d> [Shot 3] At 00:11.000, the camera cuts to Samantha standing beside Carrie beneath the enormous Martian sky. Samantha examines the completely barren landscape and gestures at the rocks surrounding them. Samantha Jones, with a confident adult female voice (S3), says: <d>[English] Forget the boots. Where are all the men?</d>

overall_soundscape: Spaceship engines and electronic controls transition into the muffled mechanical hiss of an airlock, metallic ramp movement, boots sinking into Martian soil, light suit movement, and a persistent artificial life-support hum.

non_diegetic_music: Oversized romantic-comedy trailer music with dramatic orchestral strings, electronic drums, glossy synthesizer accents, and a large brass flourish as Mars is revealed.

|

Carrie Bradshaw has shoulder-length curly blonde hair, a slim figure, glamorous makeup, and wears an extravagant designer-style SILVER SPACE SUIT with fashionable high-heeled space boots and a transparent bubble helmet. Samantha Jones has shoulder-length blonde hair, glamorous makeup, and wears a fitted METALLIC-GOLD SPACE SUIT with matching boots and a transparent bubble helmet. Both women stand on the dusty red surface of MARS beside their luxurious pink-and-silver spacecraft. The barren landscape contains red rocks, distant mountains, craters, and absolutely no other people. At the EXACT BEGINNING, Samantha is still looking around the empty landscape after asking where all the men are. A deep, gravelly male movie-trailer narrator (S1) says in an off-screen voiceover: <d>[English] They came looking for adventure...</d> while Carrie and Samantha's lips remain completely closed. [Shot 2] At 00:04.000, the camera cuts to Carrie and Samantha trudging across the red desert. Carrie struggles to walk in her ridiculous high-heeled space boots. She stops and stares down at the Martian dust covering them. Carrie Bradshaw, with a sophisticated adult female voice (S2), says: <d>[English] I hate Mars. The footing is terrible.</d> [Shot 3] At 00:09.000, the camera cuts to Samantha climbing onto a rock and scanning the horizon. Samantha Jones, with a confident adult female voice (S3), says: <d>[English] No restaurants. No cocktails. No men.</d> [Shot 4] At 00:13.000, a distant Martian rover suddenly drives over a ridge. Carrie and Samantha simultaneously turn toward it as dramatic sunlight silhouettes the approaching vehicle.

overall_soundscape: Constant spacesuit life-support hum, boots crunching through Martian soil, occasional wind-like suit vibration, rocks shifting beneath their feet, and the distant mechanical rumble of an approaching rover.

non_diegetic_music: Glossy romantic-comedy trailer score with rhythmic strings, electronic percussion, bright synthesizers, and an exaggerated orchestral swell when the mysterious rover appears.

|

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Live-action, deliberately overdramatic early-2000s romantic-comedy movie trailer titled "SEX AND THE CITY GOES TO MARS." Carrie Bradshaw has shoulder-length curly blonde hair, a slim figure, glamorous makeup, and wears an extravagant designer-style SILVER SPACE SUIT with fashionable high-heeled space boots and a transparent bubble helmet. Samantha Jones has shoulder-length blonde hair, glamorous makeup, and wears a fitted METALLIC-GOLD SPACE SUIT with matching boots and a transparent bubble helmet. Both women stand together on the dusty red surface of MARS surrounded by red rocks, distant mountains, and craters. Their luxurious pink-and-silver spacecraft is visible far behind them. At the EXACT BEGINNING, Carrie and Samantha are staring toward a Martian rover that has just appeared over a distant ridge. The rover rapidly approaches them through clouds of red dust. A deep, gravelly male movie-trailer narrator (S1) says in an off-screen voiceover: <d>[English] But sometimes... finding yourself means leaving the entire planet.</d> while Carrie and Samantha's lips remain completely closed. [Shot 2] At 00:06.000, the rover stops beside them. Its hatch opens dramatically. Carrie and Samantha eagerly lean forward, expecting someone glamorous to emerge. Instead, a tiny NASA exploration robot rolls out and mechanically scans them. Samantha's expression collapses. Samantha Jones, with a confident adult female voice (S3), says: <d>[English] I'm going back to Manhattan.</d> [Shot 3] At 00:11.000, the camera cuts extremely wide as Carrie and Samantha march back toward their spacecraft while the tiny rover follows them. Carrie struggles through the dust in her high-heeled space boots. Giant glittering movie-trailer lettering fills the Martian sky: "SEX AND THE CITY GOES TO MARS." The deep male narrator (S1) says in an off-screen voiceover: <d>[English] Coming soon... unfortunately.</d> while Carrie and Samantha's lips remain completely closed.

overall_soundscape: Martian soil crunches beneath their boots, the rover motor whines, mechanical servos move, the spacecraft hums in the distance, and the women's suits produce subtle life-support and fabric sounds.

non_diegetic_music: Bombastic romantic-comedy trailer music with sweeping strings, glossy synthesizers, electronic drums, triumphant brass, and an excessively large orchestral ending beneath the final title.

nodes.title: H3 MOTION CONTEXT - QUICK START
widgets_values:
H3 MOTION CONTEXT + REFERENCE MODE - QUICK START

Same chaining as the T2V setup, with reference images, video or audio
steering the look. Your references are kept and the continuation audio
is added alongside them. Nothing to configure for that.

Needs H3 Motion Context from August 2026 or later. Older versions
refused to run reference mode and chaining together.

WIRING:
MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo -> H3 Motion Context -> guider / sampler
References go on the reference node as usual. Motion Context sits after
it and leaves them alone.

FIRST CLIP OF A CHAIN:
- Mute/bypass the H3 Motion Context group
- Set Save Latent clip_index to 1 and generate as normal
  (the workflow ships wired for clip 2: Load = 1, Save = 2)

EVERY CLIP AFTER THAT:
- Unmute everything
- Load Latent clip_index = the clip to CONTINUE FROM
- Save Latent clip_index = the clip you are making NOW
- Keep the same references wired as the previous clip

Retry and index handling are identical to the T2V note above.

SETTINGS THAT WORK (tested):
context_length "22", audio_context_length 24.
24 frames is exactly one second of sound, and any
multiple of 3 lands exactly on the audio grid.

PROMPTING IS THE HARD PART HERE. Read this bit.

The pinned frames are not a suggestion. They are re-injected at every
sampling step and the model cannot render anything else in that span.
So if the prompt for clip 2 opens describing something different from
how clip 1 ended, the model does not choose between them - it renders
BOTH. Clip 1 ends on a close-up of one character, clip 2 opens asking
for a two-shot of two others, and you get three people in the frame.

The fix: open every prompt by describing how the PREVIOUS clip ended.
Same person, same clothes, same framing, same action. Let that run for
a beat past the join, then change to whatever you actually want. The
pinned frames get a stretch of timeline that agrees with them, and the
change happens where nothing is pinned.

Give the hold something to do - a breath, a weight shift, an eyeline
change. A held framing with nothing happening in it renders as a frozen
frame and looks like the video stalled.

At 22 frames of context the pin is 0.92s, and you want a beat past that,
so plan on the change landing around 1.5 to 2 seconds in. On a 5 second
clip that is most of the first half. Longer clips are easier than a
shorter hold.

REFERENCES HAVE NO TIMING. Every reference conditions the whole clip.
There is no way to say "this one applies from two seconds in." If the
outfit, location or character changes partway through, the shot
structure and the description have to carry that on their own.

Dark Blue Headers: H3 Motion Context nodes
Green Headers: nodes that need a user input between clips

widgets_values:
subject_definitions:

<Subject 1> is ^Thor^, wearing dark Asgardian battle armor and a flowing red cape, carrying his enchanted hammer.

<Subject 2> is ^Loki^, wearing green-and-black Asgardian armor with gold details, carrying two short daggers.

<Subject 3> is Jason Voorhees, a towering silent masked horror killer wearing weathered dark work clothes and a white hockey mask, carrying a machete.

<Subject 4> is Freddy Krueger, a supernatural horror killer wearing a battered fedora and striped sweater with a bladed glove.

retention_analysis:

<Subject 1> (appears throughout): fully_preserved - ^Thor^ maintains consistent appearance, armor, cape, and hammer.

<Subject 2> (appears throughout): fully_preserved - ^Loki^ maintains consistent appearance, armor, and daggers.

<Subject 3> (appears throughout): fully_preserved - Jason Voorhees maintains his hockey mask, weathered clothing, machete, and imposing appearance.

<Subject 4> (appears throughout): fully_preserved - Freddy Krueger maintains his fedora, striped sweater, bladed glove, and supernatural appearance.

detailed_description:

[Shot 1] Horror-themed nighttime scene in an abandoned summer camp surrounded by dense fog, dead trees, decaying cabins, and flickering exterior lights. ^Thor^ walks confidently on the LEFT and ^Loki^ walks on the RIGHT toward the camera as §personal_jesus_depeche_mode§ drives the scene. Behind them, Jason Voorhees silently emerges from the fog holding his machete while Freddy Krueger appears from the darkness beside a cabin.

[Shot 2] At 00:04.000, Jason Voorhees charges from behind. ^Thor^ spins around and blocks the machete with his hammer, producing a violent metallic impact and burst of sparks. Simultaneously Freddy Krueger swipes his bladed glove toward ^Loki^, who ducks underneath it and rolls sideways through the fog.

[Shot 3] At 00:08.000, ^Thor^ drives Jason Voorhees backward with a powerful hammer strike while lightning illuminates the entire camp. ^Loki^ creates several magical duplicates of himself surrounding Freddy Krueger. Freddy Krueger aggressively slashes at the illusions as they disappear one by one in flashes of green energy. Combat remains stylized and non-gory.

^Thor^ (S1) says, <d>[English ~Thor~]Brother, these creatures are beginning to annoy me.</d>

[Shot 4] At 00:12.000, ^Loki^ steps beside ^Thor^ as Jason Voorhees and Freddy Krueger rise again through the fog behind them. ^Loki^ notices them, gives ^Thor^ an irritated look, and raises both daggers. Everyone remains silent during the final ominous beat.

overall_soundscape:

Heavy rain beginning in the distance, thunder, electrical crackling, metallic weapon impacts, machete strikes, bladed glove scraping metal, boots on wet ground, supernatural energy effects, wind through trees, and ominous camp ambience. No intelligible background speech.

non_diegetic_music:

§personal_jesus_depeche_mode§ plays continuously as the referenced background music throughout the entire 15-second horror-action clip. Combat movements and major impacts synchronize rhythmically with §personal_jesus_depeche_mode§.

detailed_description:

[Shot 1] The horror battle continues directly at the same abandoned summer camp. ^Thor^ remains on the LEFT and ^Loki^ remains on the RIGHT with mouths closed. Jason Voorhees stands several meters ahead gripping his machete while Freddy Krueger circles through thick fog behind them. §personal_jesus_depeche_mode§ continues uninterrupted.

^Loki^ looks from one horror killer to the other, then turns toward ^Thor^.

^Loki^ (S1) says, <d>[English ~Loki~]Why is it they never stay down?</d>

[Shot 2] At 00:04.500, Jason Voorhees swings his machete downward. ^Thor^ catches Jason Voorhees by the wrist, stops the attack, then hurls him backward through the wooden wall of an abandoned cabin. Splintered boards explode outward without gore.

[Shot 3] At 00:08.000, Freddy Krueger suddenly emerges from the fog directly behind ^Loki^. His bladed glove comes down, but ^Loki^ instantly disappears in a burst of green magic. ^Loki^ reappears behind Freddy Krueger and kicks him forward toward ^Thor^. ^Thor^ swings his hammer and launches Freddy Krueger through the fog with a thunderous impact.

[Shot 4] At 00:11.500, lightning repeatedly flashes as ^Thor^ and ^Loki^ walk confidently toward the camera in slow-motion synchronization with §personal_jesus_depeche_mode§. Behind them, the destroyed cabin burns dimly while Jason Voorhees slowly rises from the wreckage and Freddy Krueger's silhouette reappears deep inside the fog. ^Thor^ and ^Loki^ never look back. Both remain silent with closed mouths through the final frame.

overall_soundscape:

Thunder, heavy wind, crackling fire, hammer impacts, wood breaking, machete movement, bladed glove scraping, magical energy bursts, footsteps on wet ground, and eerie forest ambience. No intelligible background speech.

non_diegetic_music:

§personal_jesus_depeche_mode§ continues uninterrupted as the referenced background music throughout the entire 15-second horror-action clip, maintaining musical continuity from the previous prompt. The combat, lightning flashes, slow-motion walk, and major impacts synchronize with §personal_jesus_depeche_mode§.
